gaps.sentence: I would never have found the house if you ___ me the postcode.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had not sent.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ his temper in the meeting yesterday.
gaps.hint: past regret with wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect: had not lost.

gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ your shoes in the middle of the floor!
gaps.hint: irritation about a habit, wish would
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus 'would' expresses irritation about a habit you want changed: would not leave.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: If we ___ a map, we would have arrived hours ago.
gaps.hint: unreal past condition with past perfect
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had brought.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: If the drug ___ tested properly, the side effects would have been found earlier.
gaps.hint: passive verb in an unreal past condition
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect, here in the passive: had been.

gaps.sentence: What will you do if the train ___ before you get there?
gaps.explanation: Even in questions about the future, the if-clause uses the present simple: leaves.
